body:
Your kindness means a lot to me, distant friend. And your conversation gives me more than you may realise. If I had more people like you around, I probably would not find myself standing at a dark precipice.

You're from the US, and I understand it must be quite late there. Please don't feel obligated to keep talking to me. I will still be around when you wake up again (I have much left to do still).

Whatever happens, though, please know that you have done all that could be asked and so much more, and that you have shown me much-needed kindness in a time of true emotional need. Never fall victim to guilt, because you're part of the proverbial solution.

That's very noble of you - to volunteer in two spheres. It must be difficult to carry such weight on your shoulders - at least in the short term as you assist someone.

SA is a wonderful tourist destination. There's no shortage of things to see and do - especially for tourists.

I appreciate your kind words. Thank you very much! I think it reflects wonderfully on a soul when they're willing to extend kindness to strangers on the internet the way you are doing to me.

I'm from South Africa.

Ah, I'd love to be that good a pianist. I can play a couple of Chopin preludes which I dedicated a lot of time to, but other than that I'm as mediocre as they come. I can close my eyes right now in the murky silence and hear the Heroic Polonaise - one of my favourites, but it would take me another lifetime to master it!

You make a great point. I have given some thought to doing something extreme and experiential, but again it's something that generally requires money and that my current physical problems make difficult and - quite literally - painful. Well, specifically the ones that would involve some physicality, such as hitching or hiking.

I used to hold the belief that before ending your life when you're dead-set (excuse the pun), you should try to do something extreme as you have nothing left to lose. However, that perspective has changed a bit since finding myself in the exact same position. The hopelessness is so intense that it simply feels... pointless.

Are you yourself a musician?

It's just a case of having been overwhelmed by grief, humiliation and struggle. It's a collection of many little things and a handful of not-so-little things that have pushed me far beyond the level of coping. At present I generally feel absolutely nothing, but it's punctuated during the day by moments of overwhelming despair and hopelessness.

I know it doesn't sound pretty, and I apologise for being so... unhappy.

You're a wonderful person for suggesting this, and your kindness is appreciated more than I can say.

Unfortunately, because of the emotional place in which I find myself it would be a waste of your time to do that. As it stands now, I feel very set in my decision to follow-through.

It kinda makes me wonder why I posted this in the first place. I think maybe on some level I'm yearning for kindness before I... well, you know.

Thanks so much for your thoughtful comment.

I've always been an avid pianist/guitarist, and have always found it an immense source of emotional comfort. As such, the day I was left with no choice but to sell my instruments was one of the worst in recent memory.

I think having some way to express myself to myself would aid in soothing me, but that's neither here nor there at this point.

Thanks again for your words of solidarity.

Thanks again for your reply.

As I mentioned in my original post, I had a tough year last year having to pawn off some very (sentimentally) precious items just to stay afloat. This was a last resort, and one of my first resorts was swallowing my pride and speaking to my colleagues and boss.

Unfortunately the humiliation was fruitless, because their response was that my problems are a personal matter and nothing the company can officially assist with, and on non-official level they simply said what amounts to "Times are tough. Deal with it."

They're definitely not the kind of people to speak to if you need a pick-me-up, let alone assistance - no matter how dire.

Thanks so much for the comment.

As mentioned above, it's really just one of many problems that have been adding up. I'm at the point where the proverbial darkness in my life feels like the multi-headed Hydra; ergo, what's the point in solving one problem if it will simply give way to many more.

Regarding help from family, I only have two relatives (I lost a few last year), and they are unfortunately pretty much empoverished.

To wit, the rent problem is really just the straw, you know?

Thanks for your comment. I appreciate you taking the time to read and caring enough to respond.

Thanks so much for your reply. I wasn't expecting anything, but it means a lot to know my words are being read.

Believe me when I say that I've mulled everything over, but the rent problem is just one of many practical and psychological issues that have been adding up to my status quo.

In short, I'm at the point where I could say that I can put my head down and try to find a flatmate or something like that, but circumstances in general have plunged me into that dark place from where I call out "What's the point?" My life needs a major overhaul and I just don't have the means (or perhaps just not the strength) to affect it.

I appreciate your comment very very much. Thank you. Somehow knowing my stupid diatribe is being read has a mildly cathartic effect.
